traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 213 Meliaceae: trees or shrubs, mostly with hard scented wood (mahogany, cedrela), very rarely nearly herbaceous; leaves alternate, mostly pinnate; no stipules; flowers regular, mostly bisexual; stamens mostly 8 or 10, their filaments mostly joined in a tube; ovary superior, often of 3 to 5 cells; fruit a berry or capsule, rarely a drupe, the seeds sometimes winged (mahogany).

traits.sexual_system.note: Wikipedia, Meliaceae (read 2026-10-16): flowers apparently cryptically unisexual. Weighting toward dioecious inferred (Aglaia, Dysoxylum); low confidence.

traits.leaf_margin.note: DELTA, Meliaceae (read 2026-10-17): margins usually entire, at times crenate, serrate, dentate or lobed (e.g. Azadirachta, Melia serrate leaflets).

traits.fruit_type.note: DELTA Meliaceae (read 2026-10-17; ~575 spp, ~50 genera): fruit fleshy or dry, a capsule, berry or drupe, rarely a nut; no ranking. Weighted by genus size (approximate, not read this session): capsular Trichilia (~90), Guarea (~70), Turraea (~65), Dysoxylum s.l. (~80), Chisocheton, Aphanamixis and the woody-capsuled Swietenia, Khaya, Cedrela, Toona outweigh berry-like Aglaia (~120), Lansium and Walsura; drupes in Melia and Azadirachta, so raised from rarely to sometimes.
